speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and black spots in your right eye. To better assess your condition, have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a sudden shadow in your vision? REQUEST TEST: Fluorescein_Angiography

speaker: Doctor
text: The measurement results are noted as normal. Given your history of AIDS and symptoms of floaters or vision changes, could you clarify if the "black spots" have increased in number or if you see any flashes of light? REQUEST TEST: Ocular_Coagulation_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal coagulation panel helps rule out retinal vein occlusion; given your history of AIDS, have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a curtain-like shadow over your vision? REQUEST TEST: Indirect_Ophthalmoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text: The granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages around the retinal vessels are highly suggestive of retinal vasculitis, likely CMV retinitis given your AIDS history. How would you describe the current state of your vision in the right eye—is it blurred, distorted, or partially lost? REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus Photography

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.
